svg.title: From a missed backup to an alert
svg.desc: The backup producer and the monitor run independently. This path observes receipts, not restored data. The companion guide explains each stage and exception.
svg.text: From a missed backup to an alert
The backup producer and the monitor run independently. This path observes receipts, not
restored data.
EVENTBRIDGE SCHEDULED RULE
1. Invoke every 15 minutes
An enabled EventBridge rule invokes the monitoring Lambda. This is
separate from the EventBridge Scheduler jobs that collect tracker data.
LAMBDA OUTSIDE THE VPC
2. Inspect the latest completion receipts
Read database and media receipt metadata from S3 without connecting to
the anchor or depending on its NAT.
Separate nightly host jobs upload archives before writing completion receipts. They do
not invoke this monitor.
BACKUP VALIDATION
3. Check freshness and archive metadata
Check coverage, timestamps, S3 version, size and checksum metadata. A
copy older than 26 hours or an invalid newest receipt is unhealthy.
The monitor does not download archives or try a restore. A newer bad receipt cannot
be hidden by an older good one.
CLOUDWATCH
4. Evaluate each backup stream
Report health metrics. Two 15-minute alarm periods evaluate failure; missing
data is treated as breaching. The monitor shares account Lambda
concurrency.
Evaluation and service delays prevent an exact detection-time promise.
SNS → OPERATOR
5. Investigate and repair
Enabled alarm actions target the operator topic. Inspect the newest receipt,
monitor logs and producing job; repair the cause, then verify healthy checks.
Recovery uses an authorized restore procedure. The October 8 isolated database
rehearsal measured 7m11s total, not application recovery time.
A healthy monitor is not a restore test, an inbox-delivery test or automatic failover.
